Plot a Crop Rotation Network Diagram

Source: R/functions.R
plot_rotation_network.Rd

Render an interactive node-link diagram of crop rotation transitions (in the spirit of the network diagrams in Nowak et al., 2022, Agricultural Systems 199:103402), using a dependency-free two-ring layout: the most important crops (by total involved area) are placed on an inner ring, the rest on an outer ring. Edge width and node size scale with area; monoculture continuation (a crop following itself) is drawn as a small dotted loop at the node instead of an edge.

plot_rotation_network(
  edge_df,
  crop_colors = NULL,
  min_share = 5e-04,
  show_selfloops = TRUE,
  r_min = 0.6,
  r_max = 3
)

Arguments

edge_df

Data frame from compute_transition_matrix() with columns source, target, area_km2, probability.

crop_colors

Named character vector mapping crop names to hex colors. Default NULL (all nodes/edges use a single fallback color).

min_share

Numeric between 0 and 1: edges below this share of total transitioned area are hidden (nodes are always kept). Default 0.0005 (0.05%).

show_selfloops

Logical: draw monoculture-continuation loops. Default TRUE.

r_min

Numeric: distance from the center for the single most important node (largest total involved area). Default 0.6.

r_max

Numeric: distance from the center for the least important node. Default 3.0.

Value

A plotly object.

Details

Nodes are placed on a phyllotaxis ("sunflower seed") spiral: radius grows smoothly with importance rank (sqrt spacing, so ring density stays roughly even) and angle advances by the golden angle (\(\pi(3-\sqrt5)\), \(\approx\)137.5°) at each step, so there is no hard cutoff between "important" and "unimportant" crops – the most involved crop sits at r_min, the least involved at r_max, with every other crop graduated continuously in between.
